opening.argument: The video provides concrete technical instruction, explaining that character encoding assigns binary values to readable characters and illustrating the process with an ASCII example mapping lowercase “a” to a binary representation. It then connects UTF-8 to Unicode, introduces RGB as a computer color model, and explains how combinations of zeros and ones represent computer content. citations.quote: Character encoding is used to assign our binary values to characters so that we as humans can read them.
UTF-8 is built off the Unicode standard.
